summary.text: Suitor from Same on Cephallenia in Apollodorus' island catalogue — slain in the mnesterophonia when the swineherd Eumaeus drove his spear into him among the last cast of the wooers.

story.text: Apollodorus names Elatus among the twenty-three wooers who came from Same against Odysseus' house, listed after Pisander and before Ctesippus in the Epitome catalogue.

When the returned king and his company hurled their sharp spears with sure aim, Odysseus smote Demoptolemus, Telemachus Euryades, and the swineherd Eumaeus Elatus — so the suitor from Same fell in the same moment as the others bit the vast floor with their teeth.
Not to be confused with Elatus son of Arcas, Elatus the Trojan slain at Pedasus in the Iliad, or other Elatus figures in Greek myth.
